maria: Heads up — noticed numeric blowups in paged-attn during KV warmup on a long-seq workload (seq=8192). outputs start spiking to inf/NaN after ~30k tokens. :grimacing:
jonah: Ugh. Is this the fused flash variant or the paged fallback?
sara: We were running 'flash-paged-v2' with fp16 + per-head KV packing heuristics. Kernel selection chose fused path for shorter prefixes then switched when KV pages filled up.
maria: Right — the switch seems to cross a precision tipping point. Logs show softmax exponentials exceeding 1e38 before clamp, then exp->inf. Snippet from trace:
```
[2024-05-12 16:03:12] kernel=flash-paged-v2 mode=fp16 seq=8192 head=64 max_qk=1.2e5 softmax_max=88.1 -> exp overflow
[2024-05-12 16:03:12] fallback -> stable-bf16-kernel
[2024-05-12 16:03:12] result contains NaNs: 423 / 65536 tokens
```
alex: Do we have perf counters/profiler for the exact moment of switchover? Could be batching heuristics that suddenly increase effective sequence length per microbatch.
jonah: I pulled an nvprof summary. The fused kernel was ~1.35x faster normally, but the stable-bf16 fallback is 0.6x of fused. Timeline shows a burst where batch sizes coalesced (autoscaler burst), causing larger concat batches.
sara: Here's a tiny repro script I used (synthetic):
```python
# synth to reproduce overflow
q = torch.randn(8, 64, 8192, dtype=torch.float16, device='cuda')
k = q.clone()
# force kv warmup pages to fill
out = run_flash_paged(q, k, use_fused=True)
```
maria: Observations:
- The softmax instability correlates with max(QK) per head > 1e4 (fp16 saturates)
- When we force per-head scaling (divide by max_qk) the NaNs disappear but outputs diverge numerically (~1e-3) compared to bf16 stable kernel
- The kernel selection logic doesn't currently consider dynamic per-request max_qk; it only uses seq_len and head_dim thresholds
jonah: Proposed short-term mitigations:
1) Add a pre-softmax check: if max_abs(QK) > thresh_fp16 (~6e4) => switch to stable-bf16 kernel or clamp logits by log-sum-exp trick
2) Implement runtime per-head scaling: logits = logits - max(logits, dim=-1, keepdim=True) (log-sum-exp) before exp; that should avoid exp overflow
3) Make batching heuristic avoid coalescing very long sequences into the same microbatch during autoscale bursts
sara: I tested option 2 (explicit log-sum-exp max subtraction) inside the fused kernel path, still saw some overflows because subtraction itself under fp16 loses precision if the range is huge; required upcasting to fp32 for the reduction step. Performance penalty was ~8-12% but eliminated NaNs.
alex: That's consistent — the reduction (max) is numerically sensitive. If we upcast only the reduction/temp buffer to fp32 then cast back, cost is limited to extra mem traffic. Might be acceptable as fallback for extreme max_qk cases.
maria: Patching kernel-selection quickly: add a probe step that computes a cheap max_qk estimate from sampled heads (first 4 positions) to decide. If estimate > 1e4, route to bf16/upsampled reduction path.
jonah: Sample-number experiments:
- no mitigation: 423 NaNs, avg latency 19.2 ms/token
- log-sum-exp (fp32 reduce): 0 NaNs, avg latency 20.8 ms/token (+8.3%)
- force-bf16 kernel: 0 NaNs, avg latency 31.5 ms/token (+64%) but more stable variance
- per-head clamp (hard cap logits to ±40): 2 NaNs, avg latency 19.7 ms/token
sara: TL;DR: best tradeoff is dynamic fp32 reduction for softmax max and a kernel-selection probe. We should avoid always falling back to bf16 since perf hit is large.
alex: Sounds good. A few implementation notes:
- Keep the probe super cheap (sample 1-2 tokens * 8 heads) to avoid extra CUDA kernel launches in the hot path
- Telemetry: add a metric 'softmax_overflow_probe_value' and 'kernel_selector_reason' so we can correlate in console
- Add an auto-rollout flag for the new probe so we can enable for 10% traffic first
maria: I'll open a PR with the probe + fp32 reduction fallback in the fused kernel and add the telemetry. Also will add a small synthetic perf benchmark to the eng-runtime perf suite.
dev-bot: Deploy scheduled: canary (10%) -> 2024-05-13 02:00 UTC if PR approved.
jonah: One more ask — can we add a unit sensitivity test in paged-attn CI that runs random Q/K with seq up to 8192 and asserts no NaNs across fp16 path for the canary subset?
sara: Yep, will add that. Also adding a reproducible seed to help trace intermittent failures.
maria: Thanks team. If anyone has alternative ideas (per-head norm, stochastic quant clamp, or model-side prompt shortening), drop them here. :thumbsup:
alex: Might be worth adding a compile-time kernel variant that does fp16 compute but fp32 reduction for softmax; could be a new binary optimized for hot customers.
maria: Good note. For now I'll land probe + fp32 reduction fallback and the telemetry. Tracking issue: #INF-897 (internal).
